display.title: After Hurricane Sandy: The Frierdiker Rebbe's Instruction That Saved a Life
display.summary_short: After Hurricane Sandy, a Gemara teaching on why storms come, and how a grandfather's life was saved because he followed the Frierdiker Rebbe's instruction to be home early on Friday.
display.summary_long: Recorded in a school soon after Hurricane Sandy. After a staff member's announcements about washing and lunch, the storyteller opens with the Baal Shem Tov's teaching that we can learn a lesson from everything we see or hear. The Gemara tells how a sage passing a sorcerer's house during a storm asked if he knew its cause, and was told that when Hashem remembers His children suffering in golus, two tears fall into the ocean and it roars. A storm, then, is a sign that Hashem feels our pain and that the Geulah is near. Then a family story from about seventy years earlier: the storyteller's grandfather, a Chassid in Pennsylvania who sold clothing to farmers far from the city, received a letter from the Frierdiker Rebbe telling him to finish work every Friday two hours before Shabbos. He obeyed that very week, though customers begged him to stay. When he got home his wife told him a tornado had just struck where he always worked, twenty minutes after he left. The storyteller shows the class a copy of the letter.
display.lesson: Learn a lesson from everything that happens, and listen to the Rebbe's instructions right away.
